label: Can confirm
summary: Whether the confirm button of a detailed confirmation view can be used.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, which use it as the enabled state of a confirm button. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close view
summary: Closes the detailed confirmation view.
details: Going by its name only; it returns nothing. The game documents nothing more.

label: Confirm
summary: Confirms the choice shown in the detailed confirmation view.
details: Going by its name only; it returns nothing and acts when called, for example from a button click. The game documents nothing more.

label: Confirm click sound
summary: The sound played when the confirm button is clicked.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, where it feeds a button's click sound. The game documents nothing more.

label: Confirm tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the confirm button.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, where it is used as a button tooltip. The game documents nothing more.

label: Cost description
summary: A text describing what the action costs.
details: Going by its name and by similar functions on other types, which game texts print after "Cost:" or "Maintenance:". The game documents nothing more.

label: Effect description
summary: A text describing what confirming will do.
details: Going by its name and by similar functions on other types, which game texts use for effect descriptions in tooltips. The game documents nothing more.

label: Requirements description
summary: A text listing what is required before the action can be confirmed.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, where it fills a text box. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has cost
summary: Whether the action has a cost to show.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, where it decides whether a cost section is visible. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has effect
summary: Whether the action has an effect to show.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on decision windows, where it decides whether an effect section is visible. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has requirements
summary: Whether the action has requirements to show.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on similar window types, where it decides whether a requirements section is visible. The game documents nothing more.

label: This view
summary: The detailed confirmation view itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this icon
summary: The detailed raid icon itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Raid loot
summary: The amount of loot the raid shown by the map icon brings in.
details: Vanilla prints it as a whole number after "Loot:" in the map icon tooltips, both for a potential raid and for an ongoing one.

label: Raid province
summary: The province the raid icon belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads its name (GetNameNoTooltip) and its loot from it in the raid icon tooltip.

label: Raid
summary: The raid the icon shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the map icon and reads the estimated completion time from it in the ongoing raid tooltip.

label: Has raid
summary: Whether the icon has a raid attached to it.
details: Vanilla uses it with the map zoom level to switch between the simple and the detailed raid icon. That it means a raid already under way is an inference from the icon's use.

label: This icon
summary: The detailed raid icon itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this diarchy
summary: The diarchy itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Diarch
summary: The diarch of this diarchy, the character who shares power in it.
details: Vanilla texts write it as the diarchy of a character followed by GetDiarch, in a message about someone sharing power. Who exactly counts as the diarch is inferred from that text.

label: Diarchy liege
summary: The liege the diarchy belongs to.
details: Going by its name and by the HUD reading the diarchy of the player's liege; the lines that use the same name belong to characters, not to the diarchy. The game documents nothing more.

label: Diarchy name
summary: The name of the diarchy as text.
details: Going by its name and by GetName on other types, which return a display name. The game documents nothing more.

label: Power level
summary: The current power level of the diarchy, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows the number as plain text in the main HUD.

label: Scales swing
summary: The current position of the scales of power in the diarchy, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses the player's liege's diarchy for this as the value of a bar in the HUD. Together with the swing needed for the next and previous level it shows how close the diarchy is to a level change.

label: Swing for next level
summary: The scales swing value of the next power level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the upper limit of the HUD bar that shows the scales swing. Going by its name, reaching it moves the diarchy up a level.

label: Swing for previous level
summary: The scales swing value of the previous power level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the lower limit of the HUD bar that shows the scales swing. Going by its name, falling below it moves the diarchy down a level.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the diarchy is valid, as the diarchy window checks it.
details: Vanilla shows the diarchy details when true and a different part of the window (including the benefits text) when not. Reading it as "a diarchy exists" is an inference from that use.

label: This diarchy
summary: The diarchy itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this successor
summary: The diarchy successor entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Successor character
summary: The character who is a possible successor in the diarchy.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a row in the diarchy window, so the row can show that character.

label: Successor score
summary: The succession score of this successor, as a number.
details: Vanilla prints it in the diarchy window as a whole number.

label: This successor
summary: The diarchy successor entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this window
summary: The diarchy window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can change mandate
summary: Whether the mandate of the diarchy can be changed now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable and to show the mandate buttons of the diarchy window.

label: Can designate diarch
summary: Whether a diarch can be designated now.
details: Vanilla shows the designate parts of the diarchy window only when this is true, and picks between two parts by whether the list of available diarchs is open.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the diarchy window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the click of the window's close button. It returns nothing.

label: Designate diarch
summary: Designates the given character as the diarch.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click, passing a character of the window. It returns nothing. IsDesignateDiarchOnCooldown tells whether designating is blocked.

label: Alternative power levels
summary: The list of other power levels shown in the diarchy window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window, so that part can show these levels. What counts as alternative is not documented.

label: Available diarchs
summary: The characters who can be designated as diarch.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data context of two parts of the diarchy window.

label: Available mandates
summary: The mandates that can be chosen in the diarchy window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the mandate list.

label: Window character
summary: The character the window is about.
details: Vanilla checks it for being an independent ruler: some parts show only when that character is not independent.

label: Diarch aptitude
summary: A number for how apt the given character is as diarch.
details: The game's script uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name and on the sibling function that returns the same as text. The game documents nothing more.

label: Diarch aptitude text
summary: The aptitude of the given character as diarch, as text.
details: Vanilla prints it after "Overall Aptitude:" in the diarchy window.

label: Diarch aptitude tooltip
summary: The tooltip content that explains the given character's aptitude as diarch.
details: Vanilla passes the result as the data context of a tooltip in the diarchy window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the tooltip is about.

label: Diarch label
summary: The text used as the heading for the diarch in the window.
details: Vanilla puts it in a text box of the diarchy window. Going by its name, it is the word for the diarch's role.

label: Diarchy loyalty tooltip
summary: The tooltip content about the given character's loyalty in the diarchy.
details: Vanilla passes the result as the data context of a tooltip in the diarchy window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the tooltip is about.

label: Diarchy owner
summary: The ruler whose diarchy the window shows.
details: Vanilla texts read the diarch title and the diarchy type name from it, for example in "Designate as future ..." and "End ...".

label: Diarchy succession
summary: The list of entries of the diarchy succession.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the diarchy window.

label: Diarchy succession tooltip
summary: The tooltip content about the given character's place in the diarchy succession.
details: Vanilla passes the result as the data context of a tooltip in the diarchy window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the tooltip is about.

label: Displayed diarch
summary: The diarch the window currently shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for the diarch part of the window and takes its picture from it. A tooltip text refers to the case where this diarch is indisposed.

label: Displayed succession score
summary: The succession score shown in the window, as a number.
details: Vanilla prints it as text in the diarchy window. Which entry it belongs to is not documented.

label: End diarchy interaction
summary: The name of the interaction that ends the diarchy.
details: Vanilla passes it to the character functions that check, open and describe that interaction, so the "end diarchy" button works through it.

label: Level for swing
summary: The power level that belongs to a given scales swing value, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes a bar item's value and prints the level on the bar. It shows the item only when the level is above 0.

label: Mandate AI score
summary: The score the AI gives the given mandate, as a number.
details: Vanilla prints it as "Ai Score:" in the window, which looks like a debug line. Going by that label it is the value the AI weighs when choosing.

label: Modifier description
summary: A text describing the modifiers the given character gets from the diarchy.
details: Vanilla prints it after "liege gets" and "diarch gets" and shows its part of the window only when the text is not empty.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose benefits to describe.

label: Next designation text
summary: A text saying when a new regent can be named.
details: Vanilla uses it in a warning that a new regent cannot be named until that time.

label: Power level status
summary: A text about the status of the given power level.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Power level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of one power level entry.
details: Vanilla passes the entry's index in its list to this function when showing the tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of the entry in the list.

label: Qualification score
summary: How well the given mandate qualifies, as a number.
details: Vanilla prints it as "Qualification:" in the window, which looks like a debug line. What it measures is not documented.

label: Skills
summary: The list of skills shown in the diarchy window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the window. Which skills these are is not documented.

label: Swing change description
summary: A text describing what changes the scales swing.
details: Vanilla adds it under the heading of the scales of power tooltip. What it lists is inferred from its name.

label: Has active scales of power
summary: Whether the scales of power are active in this diarchy.
details: Vanilla uses it together with HasSuccession to decide which of two parts of the window shows.

label: Has succession
summary: Whether the diarchy has a succession to show.
details: Vanilla uses it together with HasActiveScalesOfPower to decide which of two parts of the window shows.

label: Is active power level
summary: Whether the given power level is the active one.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name and on the similar IsCurrentPowerLevel. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is diarch list shown
summary: Whether the list of available diarchs is open in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to hide the normal parts of the window while the list is open. The button that toggles it is ToggleAvailableDiarchs.

label: Is current power level
summary: Whether the given value is the diarchy's current power level.
details: Vanilla passes a bar item's value and shows parts of the bar only for the current one.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The value of the bar item.

label: Is designation on cooldown
summary: Whether naming a diarch is blocked by a cooldown.
details: Vanilla enables the designate buttons only when this is false, and mentions it in the designate tooltip.

label: Is liege's diarchy shown
summary: Whether the window shows the diarchy of the character's liege.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility and pressed state of the liege tab. The other tab shows the player's own diarchy.

label: Is mandate active
summary: Whether the given mandate is the active one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility and pressed state of a mandate entry in the list.

label: Are scales visible
summary: Whether the scales of power are shown.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is window visible
summary: Whether the diarchy window is open.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the barbershop view is not open.

label: Is your diarchy shown
summary: Whether the window shows the player's own diarchy.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility and pressed state of the own diarchy tab. The other tab shows the liege's diarchy.

label: This window
summary: The diarchy window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Show liege's diarchy
summary: Switches the window to the tab of the liege's diarchy.
details: Vanilla calls it from a tab button click. It returns nothing.

label: Set mandate
summary: Chooses the given mandate for the diarchy.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click on a mandate entry. It returns nothing.

label: Show your diarchy
summary: Switches the window to the tab of the player's own diarchy.
details: Vanilla calls it from a tab button click. It returns nothing.

label: Should become liege's diarch
summary: Whether the character should become the diarch of their liege.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle diarch list
summary: Opens or closes the list of available diarchs.
details: Vanilla calls it from button clicks. It returns nothing. IsAvailableDiarchsShown tells whether the list is open.

label: Will have scales of power
summary: Whether the scales of power will be active later.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this item
summary: The diplomacy item itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Confederation
summary: The confederation the diplomacy item is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the character window.

label: Diplomacy frame
summary: The number of the icon frame to show for the item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame of an icon in the character window, so it picks one picture from a strip of pictures.

label: Info text
summary: An info text about the diplomacy item.
details: Vanilla prints it as a text in the character window. What it says is not documented.

label: Left reason character
summary: The character shown on the left as the reason of the item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a character part. Going by its name, it pairs with the right reason character.

label: Right reason character
summary: The character shown on the right as the reason of the item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a character part. Going by its name, it pairs with the left reason character.

label: Struggle
summary: The struggle the diplomacy item is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the character window.

label: Target character
summary: The other character the diplomacy item is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a character part in the character window. Going by its name, the item's own character is the first side and this one the target.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the diplomacy item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the item in the character window.

label: War score fraction
summary: The war score of the item as a fraction, shown as a percentage.
details: Vanilla prints it with a percent format and an explicit plus sign. The item has a war score only when HasWarScore is true.

label: Has reason characters
summary: Whether the item has characters to show as its reason.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the part that shows them.

label: Has war score
summary: Whether the item has a war score to show.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the parts that show the war score.

label: Is confederation
summary: Whether the item is about a confederation.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the part to show and to let mouse clicks through on those rows.

label: Is struggle
summary: Whether the item is about a struggle.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick the part to show, next to the confederation check.

label: Mouse enters
summary: Reacts to the mouse pointer entering the item.
details: Vanilla calls it from the mouse-enter event of the item. It returns nothing. What it does besides that is not documented.

label: Mouse leaves
summary: Reacts to the mouse pointer leaving the item.
details: Vanilla calls it from the mouse-leave event of the item. It returns nothing. What it does besides that is not documented.

label: Click
summary: Handles a click on the diplomacy item.
details: Vanilla calls it from the click event of the item. It returns nothing. What the click does is not documented.

label: This item
summary: The diplomacy item itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this item
summary: The diplomatic notification item itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Adding finished
summary: Tells the item that its appear animation is done.
details: Vanilla calls it when the HUD notification's animation ends. It returns nothing.

label: End animation
summary: Tells the item that an animation has ended.
details: Vanilla calls it when HUD notification animations finish. It returns nothing.

label: Days until timeout
summary: The number of days left before the item runs out.
details: Vanilla shows the number (never below 0) and runs an extra display state when fewer than 30 days remain.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the notification in the HUD.

label: Interaction description
summary: A text describing the interaction behind the item.
details: Vanilla prints it as the last line of the item's tooltip, after the main tooltip and the timeout text.

label: Timeout date
summary: The date when the item runs out.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name and on the sibling timeout functions. The game documents nothing more.

label: Timeout description
summary: A text about when the item runs out.
details: Vanilla prints it as the second line of the item's tooltip, after the main tooltip.

label: Tooltip
summary: The main tooltip text of the item.
details: Vanilla prints it as the first line of the item's tooltip, above the timeout and interaction texts.

label: Is added
summary: Whether the item has finished appearing in the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger of an animation state. Going by its name, it is true after the item has been added.

label: Is adding
summary: Whether the item is just appearing in the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger of the appear animation.

label: Is bad
summary: Whether the item counts as bad news for the player.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses a type of the same name to pick one variant of a notification. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is diplomatic
summary: Whether the item is a diplomatic one.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name only. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is good
summary: Whether the item counts as good news for the player.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses a type of the same name to pick one variant of a notification. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is neutral
summary: Whether the item counts as neither good nor bad news.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses a type of the same name to pick one variant of a notification. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is removing
summary: Whether the item is just disappearing from the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the trigger of the remove animation.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the item should be shown in the HUD.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the notification.

label: Click
summary: Handles a left click on the item.
details: Vanilla calls it from the click event of the notification. It returns nothing. What the click does is not documented.

label: Right click
summary: Handles a right click on the item.
details: Vanilla calls it from the right-click event of the notification. It returns nothing. What it does is not documented.

label: Removing finished
summary: Tells the item that its disappear animation is done.
details: Vanilla calls it when the notification's remove animation ends. It returns nothing.

label: This item
summary: The diplomatic notification item itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Start animation
summary: Tells the item that an animation has started.
details: Vanilla calls it when HUD notification animations begin. It returns nothing.

label: Access these effects
summary: The displayed interaction effects themselves, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Effect from intermediary
summary: The effect that comes from the intermediary of the interaction.
details: Vanilla reads the recipient, intermediary and actor effect texts from it. The intermediary is a third party of the interaction; the game documents nothing more.

label: Main effect
summary: The main effect of the interaction.
details: Vanilla reads the recipient, intermediary and actor effect texts from it, so it describes what each side gets.

label: Has actor effects
summary: Whether the interaction has effects for the one who starts it.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the actor's effect text.

label: Has any effects
summary: Whether the interaction has any effects to show.
details: Vanilla shows an effects part when true and a replacement part when false.

label: Has intermediary effect
summary: Whether the interaction has an effect from its intermediary.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name and on GetEffectFromIntermediary. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has intermediary effects
summary: Whether the interaction has effects for its intermediary.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the intermediary's effect text, with a check whether the local player is the character.

label: Has main effect
summary: Whether the interaction has a main effect.
details: The game uses it nowhere, so this rests on the name and on GetMainEffect. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has recipient effects
summary: Whether the interaction has effects for the one who receives it.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the recipient's effect text, with a check whether the local player is the character.

label: These effects
summary: The displayed interaction effects themselves, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use their own Self, for example as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Access this window
summary: The culture divergence window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use AccessSelf as an argument. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can diverge
summary: Whether the new culture can be created now.
details: Vanilla enables the diverge button when true and shows a blocked state when false.

label: Can pay cost
summary: Whether the player can pay the cost of diverging.
details: Vanilla shows an extra part of the window when this is false.

label: Can pick pillar
summary: Whether the given culture pillar can be chosen for the new culture.
details: Vanilla shows an extra part on a pillar entry when this is false.

label: Can pick tradition
summary: Whether the given tradition can be chosen for the new culture.
details: Vanilla shows an extra part on a tradition entry when this is false.

label: Clear selected tradition
summary: Clears the tradition that is currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click. It returns nothing.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the culture divergence window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the click of a close button. It returns nothing.

label: Diverge culture
summary: Creates the new culture with the choices made in the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from the diverge button. It returns nothing. The tooltip says the player diverges from the current culture and creates a new divergent culture.

label: Color
summary: A color used by the divergence window.
details: Vanilla uses it to tint pictures and as a color in the window. Which color it is is not documented.

label: Diverge blockers
summary: A text listing what stops the player from diverging.
details: Vanilla adds it to the diverge button tooltip and prints it in the window.

label: Diverge cost breakdown
summary: A text breaking down the cost of diverging.
details: Vanilla prints it under the heading of the divergence cost tooltip.

label: Diverge cost
summary: The total cost of diverging, as text.
details: Vanilla prints it after "Cost:" and in the heading of the cost tooltip.

label: Ethos
summary: The ethos chosen for the new culture.
details: Going by its name; no line uses it on this type, and the same name on other types gives a culture's ethos. The game documents nothing more.

label: Heritage
summary: The heritage of the new culture.
details: Going by its name; no line uses it on this type, and the same name on other types gives a culture's heritage. The game documents nothing more.

label: Language
summary: The language of the new culture.
details: Going by its name; no line uses it on this type, and the same name on other types gives a culture's language. The game documents nothing more.

label: Martial pillar
summary: The martial pillar of the new culture.
details: Going by its name; no line uses it on this type, and the same name on the culture window gives a culture pillar. The game documents nothing more.

label: New culture name
summary: The name typed for the new culture.
details: Vanilla shows it next to a "Choose Name" prompt, which appears while the name is empty.

label: Pillar blockers
summary: A text saying why the given culture pillar cannot be chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip and text of a pillar entry, and enables the entry only when the text is empty.

label: Tradition blockers
summary: A text saying why the given tradition cannot be chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text and tooltip of a tradition entry.

label: Possible aesthetics
summary: The list of aesthetics the player can choose.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the divergence window.

label: Possible ethos
summary: The list of ethoi the player can choose for the new culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the divergence window.
